sections.content: How many people are "health care practice managers"?

21,780 people

were counted on the census as "health care practice managers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Healthcare practice managers direct and co-ordinate the work and resources of medical, dental and other types of healthcare practice, including veterinary practices.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "health care practice managers" there were more women than men (85.9% compared with 14.1%).

This means "health care practice managers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "other managers and proprietors".

Men made up 14.1% and women made up 85.9% of "health care practice managers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "health care practice managers" included:

  • special and additional needs education teaching professionals
  • human resources administrative occupations
  • complementary health associate professionals

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "health care practice managers", 16.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "health care practice managers" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "health care practice managers" included:

  • registered community nurses
  • residential, day and domiciliary care managers and proprietors
  • production managers and directors in mining and energy

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "health care practice managers", 8.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (77.4% compared with 22.6%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (92.1%) than self-employed (7.9%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
